candidates.reason: io_get_sqe() fetches the SQ-array index with a single READ_ONCE(ctx->sq_array[head]) (io_uring.c:1992), bounds-checks it against ctx->sq_entries (1993) and applies array_index_nospec before selecting &ctx->sq_sqes[head]; the validated value is the same local used for indexing. The function's own comment documents the subsystem-wide invariant: 'If members of the sqe are validated and then later used, it's important that those reads are done through READ_ONCE()'. No check-then-use split on this index.

io_provide_buffers_prep()/io_remove_buffers_prep() READ_ONCE every consumed scalar (fd->nbufs at 489/508, addr 512, len 513, buf_group 495/525, off 526) into locals/req-private state exactly once, then apply the range checks (tmp > MAX_BIDS_PER_BGID, overflow checks on len*nbufs, access_ok) and later io_add_buffers() consumes only the cached copies. The raw sqe-> reads at 485-486/505 are pure 'unused field must be zero' rejections, never consumed.

io_recvmsg_prep(): every consumed field is fetched once via READ_ONCE (sqe->addr, sqe->len, sqe->ioprio, sqe->msg_flags, and sqe->optlen at line 825 for the mshot limit). The raw sqe->optlen reads at 823 and 827 occur only in the mutually-exclusive 'else' branches that merely reject nonzero; a racing write can only flip which branch rejects, never make an unchecked value feed kernel state.

io_poll_remove_prep(): the consuming path for events is io_poll_parse_events() (poll.c:834-839, 'events = READ_ONCE(sqe->poll32_events)'), a single fetch; the raw sqe->poll32_events at 875 lies in the !upd->update_events branch, exclusive of the consuming upd->events assignment at 874. sqe->buf_index/splice_fd_in at 856 are reject-only. io_poll_add_prep() likewise consumes only through io_poll_parse_events().

The raw sqe->ioprio in io_init_req() ('if (!def->ioprio && sqe->ioprio) return -EINVAL;') is a capability gate for opcodes whose io_issue_defs[] entry declares no ioprio; for opcodes that do consume ioprio, the value is fetched independently and once in their own prep (e.g. io_read_prep rw.c:277 'ioprio = READ_ONCE(sqe->ioprio)' followed by ioprio_check_cap on the same local). sqe->opcode and sqe->flags at io_uring.c:1727/1729 are READ_ONCE'd once and reused from locals.

io_uring_cmd_prep(): raw sqe->__pad1 check is reject-only; consumed fields are single-fetched (sqe->uring_cmd_flags, sqe->cmd_op, sqe->buf_index). The retained ioucmd->sqe pointer initially aliases user-mapped SQ memory (line 222 'ioucmd->sqe = sqe;'), but io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy() (line 227) memcpy's it into the kernel alloc-cache copy and repoints ioucmd->sqe to it, with the SQE128 size taken from kernel ctx->flags/req->opcode, not from the SQE. This is the subsystem's equivalent of the seed's caching fix, so late re-reads by drivers see the kernel copy.

io_uring_sync_msg_ring()'s raw 'CLASS(fd, f)(sqe->fd)' reads an SQE whose origin is io_uring_register_send_msg_ring() (register.c:955) 'copy_from_user(&sqe, arg, sizeof(sqe))' into a stack-local struct io_uring_sqe; the second read is of the kernel snapshot, satisfying the single-fetch invariant.

Raw sqe->fd/flags/off/addr/rw_flags/buf_index/user_data reads in io_uring_show_fdinfo() are debug printing of in-flight SQEs; opcode is READ_ONCE'd at 109 and the raw fields never feed kernel offsets, lengths, or file indices.

mock_file.c:67/213/280 and cmd_net.c:29/56/155 dereference 'const struct io_uring_sqe *sqe = cmd->sqe;' for fields (optval/optlen/level/optname at cmd_net.c:34-40,62-65; addr/addr3 at 163-164) after io_uring_cmd_prep() left ioucmd->sqe pointing at user-mapped SQ memory. If any of these run before io_req_sqe_copy() (io_uring.c:1613/1659/1898) swaps in the kernel memcpy copy, they are direct shared-memory re-reads; verifying the ordering requires tracing io_uring_cmd() issue flow to each helper, which was not completed within this intent's budget. mock_file.c also appears non-upstream, so reachability is uncertain.

Representative of ~54 remaining raw sqe-> sites (advise.c:36/83, cancel.c:146, cmd_net.c:160, epoll.c:33/71, fs.c:56/113/165/211/257, futex.c:132-133/179-180, msg_ring.c:263, net.c:127-128/452/1259/1392/1577/1681/1736/1808/1842, openclose.c:59/223/280-281/330, poll.c:856/886, rsrc.c:417, statx.c:29, sync.c:29/57/91, timeout.c:472-474/548-550, truncate.c:27-28, waitid.c:265, kbuf.c:485-486/505, mock_file.c:79/228/287): every one is of the form 'if (field || field2 ...) return -EINVAL;' - unused-field rejection where the field is never subsequently consumed. A racing userspace write can only flip whether the request is rejected, never cause an unvalidated value to be used as an offset, length, or file index; the consumed counterparts are separately READ_ONCE'd once in the same prep function.

limitations: io_req_sqe_copy() ordering versus the first driver-side dereference of ioucmd->sqe (mock_file.c:67/213/280, cmd_net.c:29/56/155) was not verified; this is the one unresolved candidate class and a follow-up should confirm whether io_uring_cmd() issue can reach those helpers with the raw user-mapped SQE pointer
mock_file.c, bpf_filter.c, query.c and loop.c appear to be non-upstream files; only their grep-visible sqe-> accesses were reviewed, not their full bodies
sqpoll.c's own reads of ring state and out-of-tree uring_cmd driver consumers outside io_uring/ (e.g. under block/ or drivers/) were not audited
No dynamic/compile-based confirmation was performed; conclusions are from source reading of the complete prep/issue paths for each candidate
